utterance: Chloe, the urine test shows signs of a urinary tract infection (UTI). Given your symptoms—burning when you pass urine, needing to go often, and the cloudy urine—it’s very likely you have a UTI. However, because you’re sexually active and haven’t been tested for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) before, I’d like to rule out other possibilities like chlamydia or gonorrhoea, which can sometimes cause similar symptoms.
reply: I see. So I need to get tested for STIs too? I thought it was just a UTI.

utterance: Yes, it’s a good idea to test for STIs as well, especially since you’re sexually active and haven’t been tested before. Some STIs can cause symptoms like burning when you pass urine. We can do a urine test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea, and I can also offer you a swab test if you prefer. Would you like to proceed with the STI tests?
reply: Yeah, I guess that’s okay. I just want to get rid of this burning and get back to work.

utterance: I’ve ordered the STI test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea. The results will take a couple of days. In the meantime, I’ll treat you for the UTI, as the urine test confirms that. Would you like to start antibiotics today?
reply: Yeah, I’d like to start the antibiotics today. I just want to feel better and get back to work.

utterance: I’ve prescribed you a 5-day course of nitrofurantoin, 100 mg twice a day. Take it with food to reduce the chance of an upset stomach. Make sure to finish the entire course, even if your symptoms improve before then. Drink plenty of water to help flush out the infection.
reply: I’ll make sure to finish the course. I just hope it works and I don’t have to come back.

utterance: If your symptoms don’t improve in 48 hours, or if they get worse—especially if you develop a fever, back pain, or vomiting—please come back or see a doctor urgently. These could be signs of a more serious infection, like a kidney infection.
reply: I’ll keep an eye on it. If it doesn’t get better, I’ll come back.

utterance: Also, avoid sex until you’ve finished the antibiotics and your symptoms have resolved. This will help prevent spreading any potential infection to your partner. And once we get your STI test results back, we can discuss whether your partner needs testing or treatment as well.

utterance: Yes, it’s a good idea to let him know. If your STI test comes back positive, he’ll need to be tested and treated too. For now, focus on finishing the antibiotics and staying hydrated. Do you have any other questions or concerns?
